name: artipub
headline: artipub cross-platform publishing api
short_description: artipub: Simplify your cross-platform article publishing with a straightforward API. Publish content to blogs, social media, and more without manual intervention. Perfect for content creators looking to expand their reach effortlessly.
author: artipub

sections.overview:
ArtiPub is a tool library that automates the process of publishing Markdown articles across multiple content platforms. It provides a simple API that eliminates the need to manually publish to each platform individually. The tool handles common publishing challenges like image optimization, URL replacement, and content adaptation automatically. ArtiPub supports mainstream platforms such as Notion, Medium, and Dev.to, and is designed for content creators who want to expand their reach without repetitive manual work. The project is fully open source and extensible through middleware and plugins for fine-grained control over the publishing workflow.
Publish a Markdown article simultaneously to Notion, Medium, and Dev.to
Automatically optimize and upload local images in Markdown before publishing
Distribute blog content across multiple platforms without manual copying
Regenerate and republish modified Markdown content to multiple platforms
sections.setup:
No install command available. Check the GitHub repository for manual installation instructions.
`git clone https://github.com/artipub/artipub`
sections.usage:
```
Use artipub to publish the following article: '[ARTICLE_TITLE]' to these platforms: [PLATFORM_LIST]. Format the content for each platform's requirements, including [OPTIONAL_CUSTOMIZATIONS]. Schedule the posts for [PREFERRED_DATE_TIME] and include [HASHTAGS_OR_TAGS] where applicable.
```
Copy

```
Here’s the cross-platform publishing plan for your article titled *"The Future of Remote Work in 2024"*:

**LinkedIn Post (Formatted):**
🚀 **The Future of Remote Work in 2024**

Remote work isn’t just a trend—it’s the new standard. Companies that embrace flexibility see 21% higher productivity and 30% lower turnover. But what does this mean for leadership, culture, and technology?

🔹 Key trends: Hybrid models, AI-driven collaboration tools, and employee well-being priorities.

📖 Read the full article: [LINK]

#RemoteWork #FutureOfWork #Leadership #Productivity

**Twitter/X (Formatted):**
Remote work isn’t just a trend—it’s the new standard. Companies embracing flexibility see 21% higher productivity. What does this mean for leadership? 🧵👇
[LINK]

#RemoteWork #FutureOfWork

**Medium (Formatted):**
Title: The Future of Remote Work in 2024: Trends, Challenges, and Opportunities

Subtitle: How companies are adapting to the new normal with hybrid models and AI tools.

Body: [Full article text, optimized for Medium’s formatting with subheadings, images, and a clear call-to-action.]

**Instagram (Formatted):**
📸 *Image: A split-screen of a home office and a bustling corporate office.*
Caption: "Remote work isn’t just a trend—it’s the new standard. 💼✨ Companies embracing flexibility see 21% higher productivity. What’s your take? Drop a 🔥 in the comments! #RemoteWork #FutureOfWork"

**Schedule:**
- LinkedIn: June 10, 2024, at 9:00 AM EST
- Twitter/X: June 10, 2024, at 10:30 AM EST
- Medium: June 10, 2024, at 12:00 PM EST
- Instagram: June 10, 2024, at 2:00 PM EST

All posts are optimized for each platform’s audience and engagement best practices. The article link is tracked with UTM parameters for performance analysis.
```
